subject: Theory of knowledge

objectives.name: Examine questions about knowledge critically to show how you think about knowing.
Connect questions about knowledge with situations in the world around you.
Explore how questions about knowledge connect with different areas of knowledge.
Build arguments that stay relevant, make your reasoning clear and hold together.
Support your discussion with examples and evidence that advance your argument.
Consider different viewpoints and assess their strengths and limitations.
Work through what your arguments and conclusions imply.

components.name: TOK essay
components.format: 1,600 words on a prescribed title, externally assessed; counted twice in the aggregate
components.criteriaSource: Albus IB knowledge base 6.2.2 and 6.2.3 [OFFICIAL] — TOK guide, first assessment 2022

criteria.name: Clear, coherent and critical exploration of the title
criteria.guidance: Argue about how knowledge is made, not about the topic. Specific, named, dated examples beat general ones.

components.name: TOK exhibition
components.format: 950 words on three objects, internally assessed and externally moderated
components.criteriaSource: Albus IB knowledge base 6.2.2 and 6.2.3 [OFFICIAL] — TOK guide, first assessment 2022

criteria.name: How TOK manifests in the world around us
criteria.guidance: Three specific objects, each with its own real-world context, each tied explicitly to the prompt.

notes: Both tasks are assessed against a SINGLE global instrument with five holistic levels — not lettered criteria. Modelled as one criterion each on purpose.
Essay 1,600 words, exhibition 950; examiners stop reading at the limit.
An exhibition not based on one of the 35 prescribed prompts scores zero.
The essay counts twice in the aggregate, so it is worth exactly twice the exhibition.
An E in TOK is a failing condition for the diploma regardless of total points.

The first-assessment-2022 IB subject brief hosted by Palm Beach County and Heidelberg International School’s 2026-28 handbook agree on the full TOK outline and seven assessment objectives. The objectives are unnumbered in both sources: “Albus 1” through “Albus 7” are local identifiers preserving their order, not official IB AO codes. No separate objective weightings are published. The optional themes are a choice of two, while all five areas of knowledge are required; the outline does not identify the school’s two choices.
